references.text: Legislation on taking cloaks as collateral, where God shows care for the poor by requiring that the pledge be returned before sunset
Prohibition against taking a hand mill or upper millstone as collateral, illustrating the same principle of respect for the debtor's dignity and means of livelihood
Continuation of the legislation on pledges, especially regarding returning the pledge to a poor man before nightfall
Criticism of those who take pledges without cause and strip the naked of their clothing
Reference to the wicked who take widows' oxen as collateral
Description of the righteous person who returns the pledge to the debtor
Description of the wicked one who does not return the pledge
Prophetic criticism of those who take clothing as collateral from the poor
